articles.title: RAF Abu Dhabi results: Khamzat Chimaev crushes Chris Weidman; Merab Dvalishvili wins in 90 seconds after chaotic week
articles.summary: After a week of utter chaos in Abu Dhabi, RAF's maiden voyage to the country proved to another successful night for Khamzat Chimaev and Merab Dvalishvili.
articles.body: After a week of utter chaos in Abu Dhabi, RAF's maiden voyage to the Middle Eastern country proved to another successful night for Khamzat Chimaev.In a lopsided affair, Chimaev blanked his fellow former UFC middleweight champion Chris Weidman by a 10-0 score to secure a tech fall victory and capture the RAF light heavyweight crossover championship Saturday in the main event of RAF Abu Dhabi at Etihad Arena.Chimaev and the UFC Hall of Famer tied up immediately, jockeying for position in collar tie-ups. Those sequences dominated the first period, with minimal takedowns being attempted by either man. Chimaev ultimately hit a nice dip-under trip to get Weidman belly-down for three points, then ran him out of bounds for two more points. View this post on Instagram In the second period, a wild shot from Chimaev scored, then turned into a fast scramble where he maintained control to go up by nine. Weidman's corner, however, challenged the call and lost the review, which gave Chimaev another point and the RAF title.The win is Chimaev's four straight under the RAF banner, while Weidman falls to 0-2.Ahead of match day, RAF created headlines for all the wrong reasons when former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and his friend, Saba Lazashvili, were attacked in a hotel lobby by Usman Nurmagomedov and several members of Team Khabib.Nurmagomedov, a top MMA free agent, was one of eight defendants to ultimately receive a six-month jail sentence for the incident, in addition to a fine of 300,000 UAE Dirhams (approximately $81,688) and eventual deportation from Abu Dhabi.Lazashvili, 21, instantly became a viral sensation for defending Dvalishvili and replaced Nurmagomedov's older brother — longtime Dvalishvili rival, Umar Nurmagomedov — on Saturday's RAF card against Urijah Faber. In a competitive match, Lazashvili defeated Faber via 12-7 decision, while Dvalishvili defeated Marlon Moraes via pinfall.Dvalishvili, who once again called for Nurmagomedov's release from jail in his post-fight speech, advanced his record on the RAF mats to 3-1 with the victorious performance."Umar Nurmagomedov, I will beat your a**, one-on-one... Anytime, just tell me date." Saba wants to settle the beef with Umar 🗣️ #RAFAbuDhabi (via abramidzesaba__/IG) pic.twitter.com/cnU3yVgnfP— Uncrowned (@uncrownedcombat) November 14, 2026 Merab was unfazed by this week's events 😤🇬🇪 #RAFAbuDhabi pic.twitter.com/YDZDZB7IEg— Uncrowned (@uncrownedcombat) November 14, 2026 Elsewhere on the card, Arman Tsarukyan (9-1 RAF) returned to action in the co-main event, dominating fellow MMA veteran Neiman Gracie (0-1 RAF) en route to a 10-0 tech fall shoutout, while RAF champions Kyle Dake (5-0 RAF), Kyle Snyder (5-0 RAF) and Kennedy Blades (4-0 RAF) all retained their belts with a trio of lopsided tech fall wins.Check out complete RAF Abu Dhabi results below, as well as Uncrowned's live blog.Full Results:Light heavyweight crossover championship: Khamzat Chimaev def. articles.title: FAA ground stop latest updates: Controllers’ union chief says communications with some planes were disrupted; cancellations top 5,000; Duffy blames L3Harris
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed contractor L3Harris but said officials haven’t determined whether the outage was caused by the company’s error or a faulty router. L3Harris says it’s supporting the FAA’s investigation.
articles.body: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, right, with Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford, left, and Rebecca Gay, FAA Acting Chief Technology Officer, speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Department of Transportation, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Tom Brenner)AP Photo/Tom BrennerAirlines canceled thousands more flights Saturday as they recovered from Friday’s nationwide ground stop, but the FAA said schedules should be back to normal by the end of Sunday.More than 5,000 U.S. flights had been canceled Saturday as of 2:48 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware, already past the top of the 4,000 to 5,000 that FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford predicted. Flight-tracking app Flighty said the outage has now caused more cancellations than the 2024 CrowdStrike software failure. “I do think the worst is behind us,” Bedford said, and he apologized to travelers.The FAA halted departures nationwide for more than four hours Friday, the longest ground stop since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. About 12,000 flights couldn’t be completed, Bedford said.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage began while L3Harris Technologies, which runs the network, was doing routine work to switch lines from copper wire to fiber at a remote FAA site. A router involved in the work flooded the rest of the system, disrupting communications with airplanes and radar. Duffy said officials are working to determine “whether we had incompetence” by the contractor or a faulty router. “Until I can build” a new network, he said, “I’m stuck with L3Harris.” Bedford said the review will determine whether the router was installed or configured incorrectly, or was simply defective.In a statement to Yahoo News, L3Harris said it is “supporting the FAA in its investigation” and “takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.” The company did not address Duffy’s criticism or say what went wrong.Asked why the work was done on a Friday afternoon, Duffy said work at small, remote sites is done during the day because it isn’t expected to affect the wider system. “There’ll be a reevaluation of when we do this work,” he said. Bedford said maintenance on the network is logged on paper, so officials had to search through paper records to figure out who was working where.Nick Daniels, president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, told Yahoo News that communications with some planes were disrupted during the outage and that controllers moved flights to working frequencies. Asked whether work like Friday’s should be done during the day, he said, “If the worst outcome is we lose all of our frequencies, well, then that work should be done when there’s the fewest airplanes in the sky.”The network’s problems aren’t new. A 2023 FAA-commissioned safety review called it obsolete, CBS News reported. In 2009, a technician for L3Harris’ predecessor, Harris Corp., misconfigured a router while moving the network to fiber, disrupting 129 air traffic facilities, according to a Transportation Department inspector general review.Duffy is pressing Congress for more money to replace the system. President Trump has asked for $30 billion and Duffy has said he wants $50 billion, on top of the $12.5 billion Congress approved last year. Bedford said the router swap was routine maintenance, not part of that modernization effort.New York Gov. Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign Saturday. Sen. Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois and a ranking member of an aviation subcommittee, called for an investigation.Travelers whose flights were canceled are owed a refund if they choose not to fly, and most major airlines are offering travel waivers. Airlines’ promises of hotels and meals generally cover only disruptions within their control, which doesn’t include an FAA ground stop.
